## Detailed entries

### Box Elder County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** County Commission unanimously adopted Ordinance 654 on 2026-06-10.
- **Date field:** `2026-06-10` (exact)
- **Duration:** 180-day temporary land-use regulation on data centers, data center power plants, and associated digital infrastructure in areas where the county retains land-use authority. Stops new land-use and business-license applications, building permits, administrative appeals, conditional use permits, subdivisions, zone changes, site plans, development agreements, and similar approvals. Applications formally determined complete before the effective date may proceed; incomplete covered applications are suspended.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `ut-box-elder-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Ordinance 654, Box Elder County Commission
- **What prompted it:** Adopted while the county develops updated data center regulations, in areas outside the Military Installation Development Authority's Stratos project area.
- **Affected projects:** Explicitly does not apply to the Stratos project (MIDA-controlled project area)
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-07-31; 180-day pause from 2026-06-10. County officials expressly stated it does not affect the Stratos project, because the Military Installation Development Authority (MIDA), not the county, controls land use within that project area.
- **Outcome:** —

### Cache County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** County Council suspended its rules and voted 6-0 (one member absent) to adopt Ordinance 2026-32 on 2026-06-23.
- **Date field:** `2026-06-23` (exact)
- **Duration:** Proactive 180-day moratorium on data centers and data center power plants across all zones in unincorporated Cache County, pausing covered land-use, license, permit, appeal, conditional-use, subdivision, zone-change, site-plan, development-agreement, and similar applications (applications already determined complete may continue). Directs staff and the Planning Commission to prepare permanent regulations within 150 days.

- **What prompted it:** Proactive measure; minutes state the county had received no data center inquiries and the action was not a response to a pending project.
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Status notes:** Recorded active as of 2026-07-31; county adopted the 180-day pause on 2026-06-23, and the council chair reported no inquiries about potential data centers. - **Outcome:** —

### Clearfield

- **Type:** City
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** 2026-09-08, Clearfield City Council adopted Ordinance 2026-13; the signed ordinance records four affirmative votes and Councilmember Thompson absent.
- **Date field:** `2026-09-08` (exact)
- **Duration:** 180 days from the ordinance effective date unless terminated earlier; the retained signed ordinance does not specify that date.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `ut-clearfield-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Clearfield City Ordinance 2026-13, adopted September 8, 2026, establishes a temporary land use regulation regarding data center uses. The signed ordinance states a 180-day term from its effective date; the operative restriction and effective date require further review.
- **What prompted it:** regulatory_gap; a pending zoning-determination request for a proposed data center in the Freeport Center's M-1 Manufacturing Zone (Building J8) exposed that Clearfield's code has no definition or zoning classification for 'data center,' prompting the Council to pause while it studies electrical demand, water consumption, noise, and other impacts and considers pending state legislation.
- **Affected projects:** A pending zoning-determination request (not yet a formal application) for a proposed data center in Building J8 at the Freeport Center, M-1 Manufacturing Zone; city staff's preliminary review found the use did not clearly fit existing warehouse or manufacturing classifications.
- **Status notes:** Signed Ordinance 2026-13 records September 8 adoption, four affirmative votes including King, and Thompson absent. It states 180 days from its effective date unless terminated earlier. The five-page text does not specify that date or include an express operative prohibition section; its title, findings and city adoption notice describe a temporary data-center land-use regulation. Precise restriction, operative interval and later force require review. [VERIFY: operative interval, later amendments/extensions/repeal, judicial developments and current legal force.]
- **Outcome:** Clearfield City Council adopted a 180-day moratorium on data center development after a zoning-determination request exposed a gap in the city's zoning code.

### Grand County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** County Commission voted 7-0 on 2026-07-07 to adopt a temporary land use regulation, effective immediately.
- **Date field:** `2026-07-07` (exact)
- **Duration:** Pause for up to 180 days on acceptance and processing of applications for data centers, data center power plants, and associated digital infrastructure. Planning and Zoning Director Andrew Jackson said no data center application was pending and the county code lacked a data center definition and standards addressing water, power, noise, lighting, and visual impacts.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `ut-grand-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Item 15, 'Ordinance - Temporary land use regulation - Data Centers,' approved 7-0 (Commissioner Bill Winfield's motion seconded, all present commissioners voting yes) at the Grand County Commission's July 7, 2026 regular meeting, per the county's own signed meeting minutes; pauses acceptance and processing of applications, permits, and licenses for data centers, data center power plants, and associated digital infrastructure for up to 180 days. County staff refer to the instrument as a 'temporary land use regulation' rather than 'moratorium' on the advice of the county's land-use attorney, though it functions as a moratorium. No separately numbered ordinance document (e.g., 'Ordinance No. ___') was found; the minutes themselves are the primary record of adoption.
- **What prompted it:** County code lacked a data center definition and standards addressing water, power, noise, lighting, and visual impacts; no data center application was pending.
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Status notes:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Confirmed via Grand County's own signed July 7, 2026 Commission meeting minutes: the Commission voted 7-0 to adopt the ordinance/temporary land use regulation pausing acceptance and processing of data center, data center power plant, and associated digital infrastructure applications for up to 180 days (through approximately January 3, 2027), effective immediately. Staff described it as 'not a ban' and confirmed no data center applications were pending at adoption. No extension, replacement, or rescission was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23. A distinct, unrelated moratorium reported by SkyHiNews.com running through June 2027 refers to Grand County, Colorado, not this Grand County, Utah row.
- **Outcome:** —

### Iron County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** County Commission approved Ordinance 2026-13 by a 2-0 vote (Commissioner Paul Cozzens absent) on 2026-05-26.

- **Duration:** 180 days. Bars acceptance or processing of new applications for data centers, data center power plants, and solar power plants while the county develops updated regulations. Complete applications were exempt (the Pronghorn/Antelope Data Center application was identified as complete and exempt); incomplete pending applications were suspended (the BrightNight Red Butte application was placed on hold).

- **Sectors:** data center, solar
- **Record ID:** `ut-iron-county-2026`

- **What prompted it:** Adopted while the county develops updated data center and solar power plant regulations.
- **Affected projects:** Pronghorn Development LLC's Antelope Data Center application (deemed complete, exempt); BrightNight's Red Butte Energy and Data Center Campus application (incomplete, placed on hold)
- **Status notes:** Recorded active as of 2026-07-31; the county reports adoption on 2026-05-26. The county form ties the 180-day period to passage and publication; the publication date is unverified. The Antelope Data Center conditional-use permit was approved on 2026-06-04 and county staff say its application was deemed complete before the moratorium took effect, so it was not blocked. An August 10 agenda considered a BESS exception; a secondary report attributes adoption to an August 10 vote, though its page header is dated August 9; the adopted amendment has not been independently verified.

### SB0231 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `ut-sb0231-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Scott D. Sandall; R
- **Status:** Passed Senate 2026-03-03 (27-0-2) after substitution from S1 to S2. House read the bill on its 3rd Reading Calendar and circled it by voice vote 2026-03-06; it returned to House Rules, its enacting clause was struck, and the Senate filed it as not passed late on March6. No House final-passage vote is recorded in the retained history; the procedural voice vote is not bill passage.
- **Provisions:** Introduced Energy User Property Tax Amendments proposed statewide distribution of large-load property-tax revenue through population-based county shares, tax-increment agreement restrictions with a pre-May6,2026 agreement exception, and customer-address notice within30days of commission approval of a large-load contract. S1 replaced that program with limits on private pipeline eminent domain serving principally own-use/beneficiary energy generation and a property-owner evidence provision shifting rebuttal to clear-and-convincing proof. Senate-passed S2 omitted the primarily/objective-evidence wording and separate proof-shifting section, and added easement exceptions for pipelines within existing utility easements or immediately adjacent and parallel to existing utility lines; pipelines within or immediately adjacent and parallel to existing/planned roadways; and pipelines able to serve more than one customer on completion. S2 retained prospective/pending-action coverage. These were failed proposals, not current requirements; specific data-center applicability remains unestablished.
- **Mechanism / scope:** other; utility_grid
- **Legal effect:** failed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://le.utah.gov/~2026/bills/static/SB0231.html>)
